raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview Builds on #63210 (typed-array staging in `StagedWriteTensor`), which is the first commit here. Only the last commit belongs to this PR. That commit stages numpy and `array.array` contents by reference, concatenates all staged contents straight into a UVA buffer slot, and has the write kernel read them through UVA for GPU-resident targets too. Ideas are taken from #59908 (@benenzhu) and #62702 (@Juntian777), who are credited as co-authors. ## Claims - On both GB200 and MI350X, `apply_write` is faster than main and than #63210 alone, in GPU time and in host time, across every shape measured. This includes the small block-table writes, where #63210 alone was slightly slower than main. - A numpy array or `array.array` is staged without a copy. For example, mrope positions or a 131k-token `array('i')` take about 65µs to stage and apply on GB200, against 4–13ms on main. - The write kernel reads staged contents through UVA for GPU-resident targets too, not only UVA targets. This removes the per-apply pinned allocation and `cudaMemcpyAsync`. Without pinned memory, the existing `NonUvaBuffer` fallback copies into a preallocated device buffer. - There is no new option. All existing callers get the same values in the same rows. ## Validation **Tests** (`tests/kernels/core/test_uva.py` and `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py`): | Platform | GPUs visible | Runs | Result | |---|---|---|---| | GB200 | 2 | 3 | 50 passed, 4 skipped each | | MI350X, ROCm 7.2.2 | 1 | 4 | 25 passed, 22 skipped each | On ROCm, `test_gpu_block_table.py` is skipped as CUDA-only. **GPU time per `apply_write`**, in µs at p50 (p10–p90 in the notes below), int32 target resident on the GPU: | case | GB200 main | GB200 #63210 | GB200 this | MI350X main | MI350X #63210 | MI350X this | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | block table 256 × 1 | 19.1 | 10.9 | 6.8 | 12.5 | 12.4 | 6.5 | | block table 32 × 64 | 10.9 | 12.2 | 6.8 | 12.4 | 12.4 | 6.3 | | dense 1 × 8192 | 19.0 | 19.1 | 8.8 | 26.0 | 26.0 | 6.3 | | dense 8 × 8192 | 19.1 | 19.1 | 8.9 | 31.1 | 31.3 | 10.2 | | dense 1 × 131056 | 19.1 | 19.1 | 9.9 | 35.8 | 35.8 | 14.7 | **Host time per stage + apply**, in µs (median): | case | GB200 main | GB200 #63210 | GB200 this | MI350X main | MI350X #63210 | MI350X this | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | block table 256 × 1-int lists | 168 | 179 | 131 | 76 | 75 | 67 | | block table 32 × 64-int lists | 177 | 122 | 79 | 81 | 48 | 40 | | block table 32 × 64, 4 groups (fused) | 527 | 247 | 201 | 272 | 127 | 118 | | `all_token_ids` (GPU target), 1 × 131k list | 5413 | 1384 | 1327 | 3009 | 918 | 910 | | `all_token_ids`, 1 × 131k `array('i')` | 4076 | 65 | 64 | 3502 | 27 | 26 | | mrope positions, 1 × 131k | 13097 | 176 | 178 | 11790 | 65 | 64 |
Method - **Builds compared:** all three `buffer_utils.py` versions (main, #63210, and this PR) are loaded side by side in one process, on one GPU. - **GPU time:** 1. Stage the writes; this part is not timed. 2. Enqueue `torch.cuda._sleep` so the GPU is busy. 3. Record a CUDA event, call `apply_write`, and record a second event. 4. Keep the sample only if the GPU was still sleeping when the host finished enqueueing. This measures what `apply_write` enqueues back to back (the H2D copy plus the kernel, or just the kernel), without host launch gaps. Each case uses 600 samples. - **Host time:** median wall time of stage + apply, with `synchronize()` excluded from the "host" number. - **Distributions:** on GB200 the H2D variants are bimodal, at about 11µs and about 19µs. With UVA contents, p10–p90 stays within about 2µs.
There is no end-to-end serving benchmark yet. The gains are on the step-critical path of MRV2 input preparation (block-table updates every step, prompt staging on admission). They are microbenchmarks only, so the effect on whole steps is unmeasured. ## Details - **Buffer inputs by reference.** - `stage_write` keeps an `np.ndarray` or `array.array` as its own chunk, closing off any pending list contents into a chunk first. - Lists still go through `array.fromlist`, and other iterables through `extend`. - `apply_write` does one `np.concatenate(chunks, out=uva_slot, casting="unsafe")`. - Callers must not modify a staged buffer before `apply_write`. Values are cast to the target dtype, and out-of-range values wrap. Both behaviours are documented in the docstring. - `rope.py` now passes `prefill_positions[i].numpy()` instead of `.tolist()`. - **Direct copy into UVA** (after #59908). `UvaBufferPool._next_buf` and `copy_chunks_to_uva` write the concatenation straight into the pool slot, with no intermediate contents buffer. - **UVA contents for GPU targets.** - Before: #63210, like main, copied contents with `async_tensor_h2d` for GPU-resident targets. That costs about 25µs of host time per apply (a pinned allocation plus `cudaMemcpyAsync`) and about 10–25µs of GPU time for the copy engine. - Now: the kernel reads the pinned contents directly. Both approaches cross the link once and run serialized on the same stream. The UVA read was cheaper on NVLink-C2C (GB200) and on PCIe (MI350X) alike, including for 512KB dense writes. - `FusedStagedWriter` gets a UVA contents pool for the same reason. - **No rollback in `stage_write`.** The try/except from #63210 is removed: `fromlist` is already atomic, and a failed staging call is a caller bug. - **Typecode map.** `TORCH_DTYPE_TO_ARRAY_TYPECODE` moves to `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py`, next to `TORCH_DTYPE_TO_NUMPY_DTYPE`. - **Interaction with #62702.** #62702 keeps prompt token ids as int32 `array`s end to end. With this PR, those arrays are staged into `all_token_ids` without any copy. - **Tests.** - `test_staged_write_input_types`: interleaves lists, ranges, int64 and strided int32 arrays, `array('i')`, empty arrays and `stage_write_elem`. - `test_staged_write_uses_uva_contents`: now covers both target kinds, pinned to the target's device. Without that, a leftover current device from an earlier test makes the GPU-target case fail when two GPUs are visible. - `test_staged_write_without_uva`: forces the `NonUvaBuffer` fallback through `apply_write` and through `FusedStagedWriter`. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

+@pytest.mark.skipif(not is_uva_available(), reason="UVA is not available.")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("uva_target", [False, True])
+def test_staged_write_input_types(uva_target):
+    """Lists, other iterables, arrays and NumPy arrays of any dtype stage the same
+    values, in any interleaving."""
+    device = torch.device(f"{DEVICE_TYPE}:0")
+    with torch.accelerator.device_index(device.index):
+        state = StagedWriteTensor(
+            (5, 8), torch.int32, device, uva_instead_of_gpu=uva_target
+        )
+        # Twice, to reuse the staging state and both pool slots.
+        for b in (0, 100):
+            state.stage_write(0, 1, [b + 1, b + 2, b + 3])
+            state.stage_write(2, 0, np.arange(b + 6, b + 9, dtype=np.int64))
+            state.stage_write(1, 2, range(b + 4, b + 6))
+            # Non-contiguous int32 view.
+            state.stage_write(3, 3, np.arange(b + 9, b + 13, dtype=np.int32)[::2])
+            state.stage_write(3, 0, np.array([], dtype=np.int64))
+            state.stage_write_elem(4, b + 14)
+            state.stage_write(4, 1, array.array("i", [b + 15, b + 16]))
+            state.stage_write(4, 3, [b + 17])
+            state.apply_write()
+            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+
+            assert state.gpu.tolist() == [
+                [0, b + 1, b + 2, b + 3, 0, 0, 0, 0],
+                [0, 0, b + 4, b + 5, 0, 0, 0, 0],
+                [b + 6, b + 7, b + 8, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
+                [0, 0, 0, b + 9, b + 11, 0, 0, 0],
+                [b + 14, b + 15, b + 16, b + 17, 0, 0, 0, 0],
+            ]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.accelerator.is_available(), reason="No accelerator.")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("fused", [False, True])
+def test_staged_write_without_uva(monkeypatch, fused):
+    """Without pinned memory, staged writes go through NonUvaBuffer copies."""
+    monkeypatch.setattr(buffer_utils, "is_uva_available", lambda: False)
+    device = torch.device(f"{DEVICE_TYPE}:0")
+    with torch.accelerator.device_index(device.index):
+        # uva_instead_of_gpu falls back to a device-resident target.
+        tables = [
+            StagedWriteTensor((3, 2048), torch.int32, device, uva_instead_of_gpu=uva)
+            for uva in (False, True)
+        ]
+        for t in tables:
+            assert t.gpu.device.type == DEVICE_TYPE
+            assert isinstance(t.write_contents._uva_bufs[0], buffer_utils.NonUvaBuffer)
+        writer = buffer_utils.FusedStagedWriter(device, max_writes=8)
+        ptrs = torch.tensor(
+            [t.gpu.data_ptr() for t in tables], dtype=torch.uint64, device=device
+        )
+        strides = torch.tensor(
+            [t.gpu.stride(0) for t in tables], dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+        )
+        expected = [torch.zeros((3, 2048), dtype=torch.int32) for _ in tables]
+        # Rounds of varying size reuse and grow both pool slots.
+        for step, length in enumerate([5, 2000, 3, 1500]):
+            for i, t in enumerate(tables):
+                base = step * 10000 + i * 5000
+                values = np.arange(base, base + length, dtype=np.int64)
+                t.stage_write(0, 1, values.tolist())
+                t.stage_write(1, 0, values)
+                t.stage_write(2, 3, array.array("i", [base, base + 1]))
+                t.stage_write_elem(2, base + 2)
+                expected[i][0, 1 : 1 + length] = torch.from_numpy(values)
+                expected[i][1, :length] = torch.from_numpy(values)
+                expected[i][2, 3:5] = torch.tensor([base, base + 1])
+                expected[i][2, 0] = base + 2
+            if fused:
+                writer.apply(tables, ptrs, strides)
+            else:
+                for t in tables:
+                    t.apply_write()
+            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+            for t, ref in zip(tables, expected):
+                torch.testing.assert_close(t.gpu.cpu(), ref, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
